items.title: Russia says it intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones in four hours

featured_image.name: Russia's drone revolution heaps pressure on Ukrainian ...

items.description:
Russia's Defense Ministry said on Sunday that its air defense units intercepted 170 Ukrainian drones over central and southern Russia within a four-hour window, in what officials described as a higher-than-average wave of aerial attacks that included two drones headed for Moscow.[1][2]

The interceptions took place between 2 p.m. and 6 p.m. Moscow time (1100-1500 GMT), according to the ministry. The Bryansk region, which borders Ukraine, recorded the highest concentration with 73 drones intercepted. No damage or casualties were reported.[3][4]

items.title: US, Israel weigh special forces raid to seize Iran's enriched uranium

featured_image.name: U.S. weighs sending special forces to seize Iran's nuclear ...

items.description: The United States and Israel have discussed sending special forces into Iran to secure its stockpile of highly enriched uranium at a later stage of the ongoing war, Axios reported Saturday, citing four sources with knowledge of the discussions. The operation, one of the most sensitive options under consideration, would require American or Israeli troops to enter heavily fortified underground nuclear facilities on Iranian soil.[1][2]

items.title: UAE denies Israeli reports it struck Iranian desalination plant

featured_image.name: UAE denies striking Iran water facility after Gulf attacks ...

items.description: Multiple Israeli media outlets reported Sunday that the United Arab Emirates carried out its first offensive strike against Iran, targeting a desalination facility — a claim the UAE swiftly and categorically denied, calling the reports "fake news" and "inappropriate."

items.title: Israel says it dropped 7,500 bombs on Iran in first week of war

featured_image.name: Netanyahu tells Iranians freedom is near as Israel hits ...

items.description:
The Israeli military announced that it has conducted approximately 3,400 strikes across Iran and dropped roughly 7,500 munitions since the war began on February 28, marking a dramatic escalation in the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign dubbed Operation Roaring Lion.[1][2]

IDF Spokesman Brig. Gen. Effie Defrin detailed the scope of the campaign in a press conference on Friday, noting that the munitions total is "twice the number dropped during Operation Rising Lion," referring to Israel's 12-day war with Iran in June 2025. The IDF also said more than 150 Iranian air defense systems have been disabled since the operation's launch.[2][1]

items.title: Saudi Arabia reports first deaths as projectile hits Al-Kharj

featured_image.name: Military projectile hits residential site in Al-Kharj, two ...

items.description:
A military projectile struck a residential compound in Al-Kharj, Saudi Arabia, on Sunday, killing two foreign nationals and injuring 12 others in what officials confirmed were the kingdom's first civilian deaths since the US-Israel-Iran war began on February 28.

The Saudi Civil Defense said the projectile hit a residential site belonging to a maintenance and cleaning company, killing one Indian national and one Bangladeshi national. The 12 injured were all Bangladeshi residents. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier on Sunday that they had targeted radar systems at locations including Al-Kharj, which is home to Prince Sultan Air Base, a key US military facility that has been repeatedly targeted since the war began.[1][2][3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills 2 in Gaza amid ongoing ceasefire breaches

featured_image.name: Israeli attack across Gaza kill 14 Palestinians despite 'ceasefire'

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike killed at least two Palestinians traveling in a vehicle near Al-Azhar University in western Gaza City on Sunday, according to Reuters and local health authorities, marking the deadliest single incident in the territory since the U.S.-Israeli military operations against Iran began a week earlier.[1][2]

Medical officials said several other people in the area were also wounded in the strike. The identities of the two victims have not been confirmed. The Israeli military did not comment on the attack.[1]

items.title: Iran missile with suspected cluster warhead wounds six in central Israel

featured_image.name: 6 wounded by shrapnel, 1 seriously, as Iran fires suspected cluster warhead  missile at Israel | The Times of Israel

items.description: An Iranian ballistic missile carrying a suspected cluster warhead struck central Israel on Sunday afternoon, wounding six people at multiple impact sites across the Tel Aviv metropolitan area, as the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran entered its ninth day.

items.title: Israeli settlers murder three Palestinians in West Bank village raid

featured_image.name: Israeli Settler Attack in West Bank Kills Three Palestinians

items.description: Three Palestinians were killed and several others wounded when Israeli settlers stormed the village of Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, in an overnight attack early Sunday, marking the second deadly settler shooting in the occupied West Bank in as many days.

items.title: US Embassy in Baghdad attacked as Iran war enters second week

featured_image.name: Rocket targets Baghdad's Green Zone

items.description: Iran continued to pummel Gulf nations and US military installations with waves of missiles and drones on Saturday, March 7, as the conflict sparked by last week's joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran entered its second week with no signs of abating. The attacks, which Iran has carried out under a contingency plan dubbed "Operation Madman," have killed civilians, disrupted global energy markets, and drawn once-stable Gulf capitals into the crossfire of a widening Middle Eastern war.

items.title: Israel strikes Iran oil sites, Beirut hotel as war widens

featured_image.name: Israel hits Iran’s oil depots as clerics say consensus reached on Ayatollah successor

items.description: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran entered its second week on Sunday with no signs of abating, as Israel struck oil facilities in Tehran and targeted Iranian commanders in central Beirut while Iran pressed its missile and drone campaign against Gulf Arab states, hitting a desalination plant in Bahrain and fuel tanks at Kuwait's international airport.

items.title: Iran war puts Gulf's desalination plants at risk

featured_image.name: Chaos sown by Iran's attacks across the Persian Gulf is key to its strategy  | PBS News

items.description: As the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran enters its second week, analysts warn that the conflict's most dangerous fallout may not be disrupted oil flows but the threat to the Persian Gulf's desalinated water supply — the invisible lifeline sustaining tens of millions of people across one of the world's driest regions.

items.title: Israel strikes Iran's oil facilities as crude tops $90

featured_image.name: Oil surges for second day, Brent tops $83 after Iran orders Strait of Hormuz closure

items.description:
Oil prices have surged past $90 a barrel for the first time in two years as the US-Israeli war with Iran enters its ninth day, with Israeli strikes hitting Iranian oil infrastructure for the first time on Saturday and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz ground to a near-complete halt.

Brent crude rose to $92.69 per barrel on March 6, up more than 34% over the past month, according to Trading Economics. US crude benchmark West Texas Intermediate also climbed sharply, with Bloomberg reporting the biggest weekly gain on record for US oil prices. Goldman Sachs warned that oil could top $100 a barrel if disruptions persist, while Qatar's energy minister told the Financial Times that prices could reach $150 if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.[1][2][3]

items.title: Renewed MH370 search yields no findings 12 years after plane vanished

featured_image.name: Malaysia Airlines flight MH370: New update on search - 12 years after it disappeared

items.description: Twelve years to the day after Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 vanished with 239 people aboard, Malaysian authorities confirmed Sunday that a renewed deep-sea search in the southern Indian Ocean has failed to locate the missing aircraft, prompting families to call for the effort to continue.

items.title: Iranian drone damages Bahrain desalination plant as war enters ninth day

featured_image.name: Bahrain Says Iran Drone Attack Damaged Water Desalination Plant, Injured  Three

items.description:
An Iranian drone attack caused "material damage" to a water desalination plant in Bahrain on Sunday, the country's interior ministry said, marking the first time a Gulf state has reported such a strike on critical water infrastructure during the nine-day war.[1][2]

"The Iranian aggression randomly bombs civilian targets and causes material damage to a water desalination plant following an attack by a drone," Bahrain's interior ministry said in a statement.[1]

items.title: Ukraine says it halted Russia's advance toward Zaporizhzhia in three-month operation

featured_image.name: Russia's advance on Zaporizhzhia stopped by Ukraine's ...

items.description:
Ukrainian military intelligence announced on March 7 that a three-month defensive operation has halted Russia's advance toward the city of Zaporizhzhia, capping weeks of territorial gains that represent Kyiv's most successful ground campaign since the summer of 2023.

The special forces unit Tymura, operating under Ukraine's Defense Intelligence (HUR), killed or wounded more than 300 Russian soldiers and captured 39 others during the operation, HUR said. "The actions of the special forces helped stabilize the defense at positions favorable to the Ukrainian defenders and secure Zaporizhzhia," the agency stated.[1][2]

items.title: Israel targets Tehran oil sites and Mehrabad airport in new strikes

featured_image.name: Israel-Iran updates: IRGC intelligence chief, two generals killed

items.description: Pillars of flame rose above Tehran late Saturday as Israeli warplanes struck oil storage depots and refining facilities in the Iranian capital, marking the first time oil infrastructure has been targeted since the U.S.-Israeli aerial campaign began on February 28. The strikes came hours after President Donald Trump warned on Truth Social that "Today Iran will be hit very hard," threatening that "areas and groups of people that were not considered for targeting up until this moment in time" were now under consideration.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump formally recognizes Venezuela's Rodriguez government

featured_image.name: Trump warns of imminent action against Cuba at 'Shield of Americas' summit

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Saturday that the United States has "formally" and "legally" recognized the Venezuelan government led by acting President Delcy Rodríguez, deepening a relationship born from the U.S. military operation that ousted Nicolás Maduro in January.

Speaking at the Shield of the Americas Summit in Doral, Florida, Trump said the administration has "been working closely with the new president of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez," adding that "she's doing a great job working with us." He also touted a new agreement allowing the sale of Venezuelan gold and minerals to American buyers, calling it "a historic gold deal with Venezuela."[1]

items.title: Iran hits Gulf states hours after president's apology

featured_image.name: Iran fires more missiles, drones across Gulf region amid US-Israeli attacks

items.description:
Iran launched a fresh barrage of missiles and drones at Gulf Arab states on Saturday, striking targets across the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar — just hours after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian issued a televised apology to neighboring countries and pledged to halt attacks on them unless Iran was attacked from their territory.[1][2]

The contradiction between Pezeshkian's words and the continued strikes underscored deep rifts within Iran's leadership as the war with the United States and Israel entered its second week.[1]

items.title: Trump doesn't rule out ground troops in Iran

featured_image.name: Trump to attend dignified transfer of 6 fallen service members killed in Kuwait amid Iran war

items.description:
President Donald Trump on Saturday declined to rule out sending American ground forces into Iran to secure the country's stockpile of enriched uranium, saying such a move "is something we could consider later" even as the U.S. air campaign enters its second week.

Speaking to reporters aboard Air Force One after attending a dignified transfer ceremony at Dover Air Force Base for six fallen soldiers, Trump said ground troops would only be deployed "for a very good reason" but acknowledged the possibility when asked specifically about securing nuclear material believed to be stored in underground tunnels near Isfahan.[1]

"We haven't discussed it," Trump told The Guardian when asked about troops securing enriched uranium. "At some point, perhaps we will. It would be a significant step. Right now we're decimating. We haven't pursued that yet, but it's something we could consider later".[1]

items.title: Iran's hypersonic missiles test US, Israeli defenses as conflict enters second week

featured_image.name: Iran claims its Khyber hypersonic missile hit near ...

items.description: As the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran enters its second week, Iranian hypersonic and maneuverable ballistic missiles have repeatedly penetrated the layered air defense systems deployed across the region, raising urgent questions about the ability of existing Western interceptors to counter next-generation missile threats. A Chinese research paper published the same day the conflict began appears to have predicted those vulnerabilities with striking accuracy.
